sender.en: “Your grandson”, “your granddaughter”, a lawyer or a police officer

name.en: Grandparent scam: “your grandchild is in jail and needs bail”

how.en: A caller says your grandchild or another relative is in trouble: arrested, or in a car accident where someone was hurt. A second person may pretend to be a lawyer or police officer. They say bail or legal fees must be paid right away, ask you to keep it quiet, and send someone to your home to pick up the cash, or ask you to mail it or put it in a crypto ATM. Police, lawyers, judges and jails do not call people to collect money.

text.en: A caller says they are your grandchild, or calling for them, and that they are in trouble.
A “lawyer” or “officer” says bail must be paid today or they stay in jail.
You are asked not to tell the rest of the family.
Someone comes to pick up cash at your home, or you are told to use a courier or a crypto ATM.
Grandma? It’s me… I was in a car accident and a pregnant woman got hurt. The police are holding me. Please don’t tell Mom and Dad. My lawyer will call you about the bail money.

en: grandchild in jail after an accident
lawyer called about bail for my grandson

bail money in a crypto atm

en: A grandchild or relative calls in a panic and needs money now.
Someone says they are a lawyer, police officer or court official asking for bail.
You are told to keep it secret.
Someone offers to pick up cash at your home, or asks for a courier, gift cards or a crypto ATM.
Hang up and call your grandchild or their parents on a number you already have.
Bail is never collected by phone, courier or at your door. Court couriers don’t exist.
If someone is coming to pick up money, call 911.
Report it to your local police and the Canadian Anti-Fraud Centre.
